title: Prenatal exposure to insecticides and child cardiometabolic risk factors in the VHEMBE birth cohort.
ehr_evidence: We measured the serum concentration of DDT and dichlorodiphenyldichloroethylene (DDE) and urinary concentration of pyrethroid metabolites (cis-DBCA, cis-DCCA, trans-DCCA, 3-PBA) in peripartum samples collected between August 2012 and December 2013 from 637 women participating in the Venda Health Examination of Mothers, Babies and their Environment (VHEMBE), a birth cohort study based in Limpopo, South Africa.
summary: In this prospective birth cohort of 637 South African mother-child pairs, higher maternal peripartum biomarker concentrations of DDT/E and pyrethroid insecticides were inversely associated with child adiposity measures at 5 years of age, with no associations with height, weight, or blood pressure.
key_findings: Maternal concentrations of all four pyrethroid metabolites were inversely associated with child adiposity: per 10-fold higher concentration, β cis-DBCA = −0.18 (95% CI = −0.33, −0.03) for BMI z-score, β cis-DBCA = −0.57 cm (95% CI = −1.09, −0.06) for waist circumference, and β cis-DBCA = −0.75% (95% CI = −1.34, −0.17) for body fat percentage.

Inverse associations between pyrethroid metabolites and BMI z-score were present only among children of mothers with sufficient energy intake during pregnancy: β cis-DCCA = −0.43 (95% CI = −0.73, −0.14; p interaction = 0.03) and β trans-DCCA = −0.40 (95% CI = −0.67, −0.12; p interaction = 0.05).
Maternal p,p'-DDT concentrations were associated with a reduction in body fat percentage of 0.39% (95% CI = −0.76, −0.02) per 10-fold higher concentration.
Pyrethroids were not associated with child height or weight z-scores or blood pressure overall.
trans-DCCA was associated with higher height z-score among girls (β = 0.23, 95% CI = 0.05, 0.41) but not boys (β = −0.06, 95% CI = −0.25, 0.14; p interaction = 0.04).
captured_features: Maternal serum DDT/E isomer concentrations (o,p'-DDT, p,p'-DDT, o,p'-DDE, p,p'-DDE)
Urinary pyrethroid metabolite concentrations (cis-DBCA, cis-DCCA, trans-DCCA, 3-PBA)
Child height z-score, weight z-score, BMI z-score

Covariates: child sex, household food poverty, food insecurity, wealth index, maternal age/height/postdelivery weight, education, marital status, energy intake, alcohol use, HIV status, breastfeeding duration, parity, gestational age
population: 637 Black African mother-child pairs from Limpopo Province, South Africa; children assessed at 5 years of age; maternal mean age 26.4 years
exposure_domain: Insecticides (DDT/pyrethroid endocrine-disrupting chemicals from indoor residual spraying)
limitations: Exposure assessed by a single peripartum measurement, risking nondifferential measurement error and attenuation of effect estimates.
Residual and unmeasured confounding remains possible despite inverse probability weighting.
Findings may be due to chance, particularly for DDT isomers with confidence intervals including the null.
Loss to follow-up, partially addressed via inverse probability of censoring weights.
